newsitem.title: GREECE: Ecu/drs softens on forex sales, rates lower.
newsitem.headline: Ecu/drs softens on forex sales, rates lower.

text.p: Greece's yield curve shifted down about quarter of a point on forex selling by banks at the fixing that took ecu/drachma lower to 302.600 from Monday's 302.690, dealers said.
"Depos and forex forwards have eased quarter of a point across-the-board in late trade," said a trader at a state bank.
Other dealers said the interest rate easing was linked to a softer ecu against the drachma.
Dealers estimated that more than 400 million ecus and about 150 million marks were sold at the central bank fixing.
"A Swiss client who closed out a position opened a few days ago was behind today's forex selling," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
Other dealers said forex sales at the fixing had more to do with interest rate differentials than other factors.
The central bank kept its overnight offer unchanged at 13.4O percent, for large amounts,dealers said.

"The auction of FRNs and five-year fixed coupon bonds is on the back of everybody's mind," said a trader. "We have yet to hear from the finance ministry about the five-year paper and it does not help."
Greece will auction about 300 billion drachmas worth of seven-year FRNs and five-year fixed coupon bonds next week, Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis told reporters on Monday.
A finance ministry statement said 100 billion drachmas of five-year fixed coupon bonds, the first ever, will be auctioned.
The mark was quoted at 157.85/95 drachmas from Wednesday's 157.925 fix, the dollar at 237.75/85 drachmas from 238.030 and the Ecu at 302.41/51 from 302.600 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma yielded some ground today but I think it is going to make a U-turn and head higher again in the short-run," said Takis Constandatos, managing director at Eurofinance.
The National Bank of Greece, the domestic money
market's biggest player, quoted the following late rates:
